data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: The purpose of this regulation establishes the policy for ensuring that all material created, received or maintained during an employee’s employment or appointee’s tenure with the Federal Government that meets the criteria for a Federal record remains in Federal custody when an employee or appointee departs the Agency.
policy_statements.target: all material created, received or maintained during an employee’s employment or appointee’s tenure with the Federal Government that meets the criteria for a Federal record

policy_statements.source_text: It also reiterates the special consideration given to Presidential Records Retention requirements (44 U.S.C. 22).

This regulation is published in accordance with the authority vested in the Secretary of Agriculture under 44 U.S.C. 2104 and 3101; and 44 U.S.C. 35; and the delegations of authority to the Chief Information Officer (7 CFR 2.89).

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation supersedes DR 3099-001 Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees dated March 2, 2009.
cross_references: DR 3099-001 Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees

policy_statements.source_text: This regulation applies to all departing employees, contractors, volunteers and political appointees, in all agencies and staff offices of USDA regardless of the type or duration of appointment.
policy_statements.target: all departing employees, contractors, volunteers and political appointees

policy_statements.source_text: NOTE: The scope includes employees who are reassigned to new official duty locations within USDA, those who are transferred to other Federal agencies, and those who leave Federal service.
Agency officials shall apply this policy to employees, contractor personnel, volunteers, and political appointees by incorporating references in contracts or memorandums of agreement.
policy_statements.target: employees, contractor personnel, volunteers, and political appointees

policy_statements.source_text: Access Opportunity to review documents on government premises or at another agreed-upon location.
Agency Records Officer or Staff Office Records Officer The person assigned responsibility by the agency head for overseeing an agency-wide records management program.
Classified Information Information that requires protection against unauthorized disclosure in the interest of national security and that is within the scope of Executive Order 12958, as amended.
Departing Employee One who leaves or is preparing to leave the employment of USDA.
Departmental Records Officer Person responsible for the leadership, coordination, and oversight of the USDA-wide records management program.
Documentary Materials A collection term that refers to recorded information, regardless of the medium or the method or circumstances of recording. (36 CFR § 1220.18)
Employee For the purpose of this directive, an individual occupying a position as an employee of the USDA.
The term employee also includes private industry officials (also known as contract personnel) unless specifically stated otherwise.

Federal Records All books, papers, maps, photographs, machine-readable materials, or other documentary materials, regardless of physical form or characteristics, that are made or received by an agency of the United States Government under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business, and that are preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the Government or because of the informational value of data in them. (44 U.S.C. § 3301.)
Electronic communications such as electronic mail messages are included in this definition.
General Records Schedule A National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) issued schedule governing the disposition of specified records common to several or all agencies.
Field Office Records Liaison or Custodian A person responsible for overseeing a records management program in a headquarters or field office in cooperation with the agency records management officer.
Former Employee An individual who has left the employment of USDA.

Nonrecord Materials Nonrecord materials are those Federally owned informational materials that do not meet the statutory definition of records (44 U.S.C. 3301) or that have been excluded from coverage by the definition.

Excluded materials are extra copies of documents kept only for reference, stocks of publications and processed documents, and library or museum materials intended solely for reference or exhibit. (36 CFR § 1220.18).
Personal Papers Personal papers are documentary materials of a private or nonpublic character that do not relate to, or have an effect upon, the conduct of agency business.

If information about private matters and agency business appears in the same document, the document shall be copied at the time of receipt, with the personal information deleted, and treated as a Federal record.
conditions: If information about private matters and agency business appears in the same document

policy_statements.source_text: Removal Permanent removal from the custody of USDA.
This does not include the withdrawal of material for official business by authorized employees.

Senior Official Senior officials include the Secretary of Agriculture, Deputy Secretary, Under Secretaries, Deputy Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries, Deputy Assistant Secretaries, Associate Assistant Secretaries, heads of agency components and staff offices and their deputies and assistants, principal regional officials, anyone acting in any of the above positions and political appointees.
This regulation applies to all Federal employees, regardless of type of appointment.
In addition, high-level officials and appointees may be required to account for records that could be classified as documentary and/or Presidential records.
policy_statements.target: records that could be classified as documentary and/or Presidential records

policy_statements.source_text: It is the policy that within 90 days of employment, all employees including senior officials or political appointees, must be briefed regarding the types of records they will be required to protect and the different methods for meeting the Federal guidelines.
policy_statements.actor_name: all employees including senior officials or political appointees

policy_statements.source_text: Prior to leaving employment with USDA, or reporting to a new USDA duty location, all departing employees must follow the clearance procedures in accordance with the provisions of this directive.
conditions: Prior to leaving employment with USDA, or reporting to a new USDA duty location

policy_statements.source_text: A certification (see Form AD-3001, Documentary Materials Removal/Nonremoval Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement) must be made by the departing employee, contractor, volunteer or political appointee that all Federal records, regardless of media (including social media), have been identified and transferred to the records management liaison or custodian, Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative (COTR), or have been reassigned to another employee.
policy_statements.actor_name: departing employee, contractor, volunteer or political appointee
cross_references: Form AD-3001, Documentary Materials Removal/Nonremoval Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement

policy_statements.source_text: The departing employee and the appropriate Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison and Program Manager must sign the certification.
policy_statements.actor_name: departing employee and the appropriate Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison and Program Manager

policy_statements.source_text: The following guidance helps to ensure that only appropriate documentary materials may be removed.
Separation of Personal Papers. Personal papers (as defined in section 6.m) shall be clearly designated as such and shall at all times be maintained separately from the agency’s records.

Partial Federal/Personal Record. If information about personal matters and USDA business appears in the same document, the document shall be copied with the personal information deleted, and the remaining material treated as a Federal record or nonrecord material, as appropriate.
conditions: If information about personal matters and USDA business appears in the same document

policy_statements.source_text: (See section 6.m).

Use of Labeling. Documentary material labeled “personal,” “confidential,” “private,” or similarly designated, used in the transaction of public business and which meet the definition of a record, are Federal records or nonrecord materials subject to the provisions of pertinent laws and regulations.
The use of a label such as “personal” is not sufficient to determine the record status of documentary materials.
The following types of documentary materials may NEVER be removed:
Any Federal record;

The only copy of any documentary materials involved in the conduct of the affairs of USDA or any other components of the Federal Government, whether or not judged to be records (including any copy that is unique, for example, because it contains the signature or initials of the writer, reviewers, and/or concurrent parties);
Any documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) the removal of which will create such a gap in the files as to impair the completeness of essential documentation.
Indexes, or other finding aids, necessary for the use of the official files may not be removed;
The only copy of indexes or other finding aids (whether or not judged to be records) that are necessary to the use of office files;
Portions of documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute classified information;
Portions of documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute information subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552a;

Portions of other documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute information the disclosure of which is prohibited by law, such as grand jury, tax, and trade secret information.
All other types of nonpublic Federally-owned documentary materials, including privileged materials, may be removed only with specific approval from the appropriate Agency Records Officer.
conditions: only with specific approval from the appropriate Agency Records Officer
policy_statements.target: All other types of nonpublic Federally-owned documentary materials, including privileged materials

policy_statements.source_text: Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA may request the following:
Removal of or access to documentary materials that are reasonably related to the requester’s official responsibilities while an employee.
policy_statements.actor_name: Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Maintenance of assembled documentary materials for a specific period of time, not to exceed one year following departure from USDA’s employment, during which he or she may request removal or access pursuant to paragraph 6.c.(1).
policy_statements.actor_name: Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: All records, originals and copies, are under the control of USDA, regardless of how and by whom they were created or obtained.

Removal of documentary material must be approved in accordance with the preceding provisions to ensure that USDA’s ability to claim privileges in litigation, to claim Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) exemptions, and to protect sensitive and classified information.
Personal diaries, which are really private records of public activities, are private property and may be removed.

When matters dealt with in work aids such as office diaries, logs, memoranda of conferences and telephone calls are covered elsewhere by adequate records, such work aids may be removed provided they do not contain information otherwise prohibited from removal.
conditions: provided they do not contain information otherwise prohibited from removal

policy_statements.source_text: This applies to personal papers created and/or maintained on paper as well as in electronic format.
Extra reference copies may be removed under certain circumstances.
Prior to removal, it must be determined that no legal or policy reason exists that would prevent removal and that the record copy, or other necessary copies, are available in USDA.
If the copy is of a document originating with another agency, the requirements of the originating agency must be determined.

Records will not be disposed of or removed while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, subpoena, litigation or lawsuit under the FOIA or the Privacy Act, as provided for in General Records Schedule 14.
conditions: while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, subpoena, litigation or lawsuit under the FOIA or the Privacy Act

policy_statements.source_text: As the head of USDA, the Secretary of Agriculture is vested with the authority to make and preserve records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the agency. (44 U.S.C. 3101.)
policy_statements.target: records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the agency

policy_statements.source_text: The Secretary of Agriculture has delegated to the CIO oversight responsibility for the USDA-wide records disposition program (7 CFR 2.89(a)(10); 2.89(a)(11)(x)).

Within the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), the Associate CIO for Technology Planning, Architecture, and E-Government (TPA&E) is responsible for developing and managing USDA’s records management program.
policy_statements.actor_name: Associate CIO for Technology Planning, Architecture, and E-Government (TPA&E)

policy_statements.source_text: The Associate CIO carries out this responsibility in partnership with USDA’s business and technology communities.
This responsibility includes the following:

Review proposed USDA reporting and record keeping requirements, including those contained in rules and regulations, to ensure that they impose the minimum burden upon the public and have practical utility for USDA;
policy_statements.target: proposed USDA reporting and record keeping requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Assist the Office of Management and Budget in the performance of its functions assigned under the:
Data Quality Act (Pub. L. No. 106-554 § 515) and under the Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520), including review of USDA information activities,
E-Government Act of 2002, Pub. L. No. 107-347, 44 U.S.C. Chapter 36;
cross_references: E-Government Act of 2002, Pub. L. No. 107-347, 44 U.S.C. Chapter 36

policy_statements.source_text: Administer the Departmental Records Management Program.

The Departmental Records Officer, who is designated by the Associate CIO for TPA&E , is responsible for the leadership, coordination, and oversight of the USDA-wide records management program for the Office of the Secretary:
Serves as the USDA's representative with the National Archives and Records Administration, other Federal agencies, and external organizations on matters pertaining to records management.
policy_statements.target: National Archives and Records Administration, other Federal agencies, and external organizations

policy_statements.source_text: Provides leadership and guidance to the Records Officers of USDA’s mission areas, agencies, and staff offices to ensure reasonable uniformity in records management activities throughout USDA.
policy_statements.target: Records Officers of USDA’s mission areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Develops USDA-wide policies, standards, and procedures for records management.
policy_statements.target: USDA-wide policies, standards, and procedures for records management

policy_statements.source_text: Develops and implements management systems and procedures to ensure that departing employees, contractors, volunteers and political appointees do not remove Federal records from USDA custody without appropriate authorization.

Establishes procedures for the participation of mission area, agency records officers, and staff office records officers in developing new or revised agency programs, processes, systems, and procedures to ensure that adequate record keeping requirements are established and implemented.
policy_statements.target: procedures for the participation of mission area, agency records officers, and staff office records officers

policy_statements.source_text: The Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison shall:

Ensure that nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official is examined by the Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer, or Field Office Records Liaison for the purpose of providing the appropriate protection for information that is restricted from release under the Privacy Act or other statutes, regulations or executive orders;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison
policy_statements.target: nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official

policy_statements.source_text: Obtain and maintain signed form: “Documentary Materials Removal/Non-Removal Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement” (Form #AD-3001);
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the signed agreement and related documentation are retained in a centralized file by the Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer, or Field Office Agency Records Liaison; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison

policy_statements.source_text: Receive the detailed inventory list of records and nonrecords to ensure that no departing official, employee, contractor or volunteer removes records or nonrecord materials relating to any pending or contemplated civil, criminal, or administrative proceeding, FOIA or Privacy Act request or appeal, or subpoena without clearance of the Office of General Counsel (OGC) or relating to another program activity without clearance of the responsible program official.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison
policy_statements.target: detailed inventory list of records and nonrecords

policy_statements.source_text: Agency Heads and Staff Office Heads shall:

Implement policies and procedures ensuring that current and departing officials, employees, contractors or volunteers do not remove documentary materials from the custody of USDA without authorization;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Heads and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the departing employee turns over official agency records, including social media and records maintained in a home office or on employee personal computing devices such as Blackberry, hard drive, CD-ROM, flash drive or other media (including social media).
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Heads and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that each official, employees, contractors or volunteers is made aware of such policies and procedures, and that each departing individual is provided a copy of the guidance in Appendixes A and B.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Heads and Staff Office Heads

policy_statements.source_text: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Official shall:
Ensure that nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official is examined to ensure agency business and records subject to a Freedom of Information Act request are retained.
policy_statements.target: nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official

policy_statements.source_text: Privacy Act Official shall:
Ensure that nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official is examined to ensure they do not include any privacy information.
policy_statements.target: nonrecord material being removed by a departing employee or official

policy_statements.source_text: Program Managers shall:
Ensure that departing employees, contractors and volunteers departure dates are identified as soon as possible and these individuals are made aware of their records responsibilities;

Ensure that nonrecord material that is the subject of a request for removal or access by a departing individual is examined by the agency head (or his or her designee) for the purpose of providing the appropriate protection for information that is privileged or restricted from release under the Privacy Act or other statutes, regulations or executive orders;
Decide upon requests made for removal of, or access to, documentary materials other than a request that is covered under section 7.c.;
policy_statements.target: requests made for removal of, or access to, documentary materials

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure the departing or former employee’s request is for copies of or access to only documentary materials that are reasonably related to the requester’s official responsibilities while an employee;
Ensure the request by a former employee for copies of or access to documentary materials pursuant to this manual is received no more than one year after the employee leaves the USDA’s employment.
Any requests for documentary materials after such date may be submitted in accordance with the FOIA;
Obtain the signed copy of the “Documentary Materials Removal/Non-Removal Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement (Form #AD-3001)” from all departing employees, contractors or volunteers.
Ensure that the signed agreement and related documentation (including requests or authorizations for removal or access) are retained by the agency;

Approve every request submitted in writing and in sufficient detail to identify which documents may be removed or accessed, under what conditions or restrictions, and for which documents removal or access is denied.
Each decision will be provided to the requester;
Authorize removal of, or access to, documentary materials issued under section 8.b.(3) subject to concurrence with the Office of General Counsel (OGC);
Ensure the departing employee, contractor or volunteer only removes personal papers (defined in section 6.m) that have been properly segregated in accordance with section 7.b.1.
Any question as to whether materials constitute personal papers or are publicly available should be referred to the Agency Records Officer and the OGC.

Although Federal records may not be removed, departing senior officials are allowed to create a limited number of duplicate copies of unclassified documents for personal use when warranted by the level of the position, significance of the work or research.
conditions: when warranted by the level of the position, significance of the work or research

policy_statements.source_text: Such copies are considered nonrecord material and must be reviewed and approved by the Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer, or Field Office Records Liaison before they may be removed.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer, or Field Office Records Liaison

policy_statements.source_text: An accounting must be made of all nonrecord and personal papers that are removed.
Classified and Privacy Act documents may not be duplicated or removed from Federal custody.
Prior to departure, senior officials and political appointees shall identify Federal records of which they have custody.
policy_statements.target: Federal records of which they have custody

policy_statements.source_text: Records regardless of media (including social media) shall be inventoried and those on file servers, hard drives, and in electronic mail systems shall be copied and removed or reassigned.
Inactive records shall be transferred to a records management custodian and active records shall be reassigned to another employee.
All file searches for which the employee has been tasked must be completed or reassigned, such as FOIA, Congressional or litigation-related document requests.
All employees are responsible for the Federal records in their custody.
This responsibility applies to employees separating from as well as transferring to another USDA agency.
Prior to departure, employees, contractors, and volunteers shall identify Federal records for which they have custody and are responsible for any applicable procedures described herein:
Records, regardless of media (including social media) shall be inventoried and those on file servers, hard drives, and in electronic mail systems shall be copied and removed or reassigned.
Inactive records shall be transferred to a records management custodian and active records shall be reassigned to another employee.
Depending on the status of the contract, the departing contractor employee’s records shall be reassigned to another contractor or Federal employee or incorporated into USDA’s official files.
conditions: Depending on the status of the contract

policy_statements.source_text: All file searches for which the employee, contractor, or volunteer has been tasked must be completed or reassigned, such as FOIA, Congressional or litigation-related document requests.
Maintain record and nonrecord documentary material according to prescribed USDA policy and procedures.
Safeguard records until they are authorized for disposition.
conditions: until they are authorized for disposition

policy_statements.source_text: The unauthorized removal, concealment, falsification, mutilation, or disposition of official records is prohibited by law and is subject to penalty (18 U.S.C. 2071).
Clearly designate as personal those papers of a private or nonofficial nature pertaining solely to personal affairs.
Those papers shall be filed separately from the records of the office.
Report any apparent instances of unauthorized disposition to his/her supervisor and the mission area, agency, or staff office records officer.
policy_statements.target: any apparent instances of unauthorized disposition

policy_statements.source_text: Request permission to remove copies of materials prior to leaving USDA.
The request must be submitted in writing to the head of the component in which the requester is or was employed.
The request must describe the documentary materials with sufficient detail to permit their retrieval.

Departing employees should assemble the requested material and attach them to the request, or if the materials are voluminous a detailed inventory list should be attached explaining how the requested material may be readily assembled.

Meet with their Federal supervisor or Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative (COTR) and the Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer, or Field Office Records Officer prior to departing USDA.
(See Appendix B.)
The disposal of Federal records in agency custody is governed by specific provisions of Chapter 33 of Title 44, United States Code (Disposal of Records).
cross_references: Chapter 33 of Title 44, United States Code (Disposal of Records)

policy_statements.source_text: Criminal penalties are provided in 18 U.S.C. § 641 (Public Money, Property or Records) and §2071 (Concealment, Removal, or Mutilation of Records) for the unlawful removal or destruction of Federal records.

Criminal penalties are provided in 18 U.S.C. § 793 (Gathering, Transmitting or Losing Defense Information) and § 798 (Disclosure of Classified Information) for the unlawful disclosure, loss, or destruction of certain information pertaining to national defense or national security.
cross_references: 18 U.S.C. § 793 (Gathering, Transmitting or Losing Defense Information)

policy_statements.source_text: Other criminal and civil penalties may apply for unlawful disclosure of statutorily confidential information.

The Secretary is required by 44 U.S.C. § 3106 (Unlawful Removal, Destruction of Records) to notify the Archivist of the United States of any actual, impending, or threatened unlawful removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of Federal records in the custody of the Department.

extract_result.purpose: The purpose of this regulation establishes the policy for ensuring that all material created, received or maintained during an employee’s employment or appointee’s tenure with the Federal Government that meets the criteria for a Federal record remains in Federal custody when an employee or appointee departs the Agency. It also reiterates the special consideration given to Presidential Records Retention requirements (44 U.S.C. 22).

NOTE: The scope includes employees who are reassigned to new official duty locations within USDA, those who are transferred to other Federal agencies, and those who leave Federal service. Agency officials shall apply this policy to employees, contractor personnel, volunteers, and political appointees by incorporating references in contracts or memorandums of agreement.

This Departmental Regulation supersedes DR 3099-001 *Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees* dated March 2, 2009
DR 3099-001 *Records Management Policy for Departing Employees, Contractors, Volunteers and Political Appointees
This regulation applies to all departing employees, contractors, volunteers and political appointees, in all agencies and staff offices of USDA regardless of the type or duration of appointment.
all departing employees, contractors, volunteers and political appointees
NOTE:** The scope includes employees who are reassigned to new official duty locations within USDA, those who are transferred to other Federal agencies, and those who leave Federal service
Agency officials shall apply this policy to employees, contractor personnel, volunteers, and political appointees by incorporating references in contracts or memorandums of agreement.
employees, contractor personnel, volunteers, and political appointees
Access  Opportunity to review documents on government premises or at another agreed-upon location.
Agency Records Officer or Staff Office Records Officer  The person assigned responsibility by the agency head for overseeing an agency-wide records management program.
Classified Information  Information that requires protection against unauthorized disclosure in the interest of national security and that is within the scope of Executive Order 12958, as amended.
Departing Employee  One who leaves or is preparing to leave the employment of USDA.
Departmental Records Officer  Person responsible for the leadership, coordination, and oversight of the USDA-wide records management program.
Documentary Materials  A collection term that refers to recorded information, regardless of the medium or the method or circumstances of recording. (36 CFR § 1220.18)
Employee  For the purpose of this directive, an individual occupying a position as an employee of the USDA.
The term employee also includes private industry officials (also known as contract personnel) unless specifically stated otherwise.

Federal Records  All books, papers, maps, photographs, machine-readable materials, or other documentary materials, regardless of physical form or characteristics, that are made or received by an agency of the United States Government under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business, and that are preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the Government or because of the informational value of data in them. (44 U.S.C. § 3301.)
Electronic communications such as electronic mail messages are included in this definition.
General Records Schedule  A National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) issued schedule governing the disposition of specified records common to several or all agencies.

Field Office Records Liaison or Custodian  A person responsible for overseeing a records management program in a headquarters or field office in cooperation with the agency records management officer.
Former Employee  An individual who has left the employment of USDA.

Nonrecord Materials  Nonrecord materials are those Federally owned informational materials that do not meet the statutory definition of records (44 U.S.C. 3301) or that have been excluded from coverage by the definition.

Excluded materials are extra copies of documents kept only for reference, stocks of publications and processed documents, and library or museum materials intended solely for reference or exhibit. (36 CFR § 1220.18).
Personal Papers  Personal papers are documentary materials of a private or nonpublic character that do not relate to, or have an effect upon, the conduct of agency business.

If information about private matters and agency business appears in the same document, the document shall be copied at the time of receipt, with the personal information deleted, and treated as a Federal record.
If information about private matters and agency business appears in the same document
Removal  Permanent removal from the custody of USDA.
This does not include the withdrawal of material for official business by authorized employees.

Senior Official  Senior officials include the Secretary of Agriculture, Deputy Secretary, Under Secretaries, Deputy Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries, Deputy Assistant Secretaries, Associate Assistant Secretaries, heads of agency components and staff offices and their deputies and assistants, principal regional officials, anyone acting in any of the above positions and political appointees.
This regulation applies to all Federal employees, regardless of type of appointment.
In addition, high-level officials and appointees may be required to account for records that could be classified as documentary and/or Presidential records.
records that could be classified as documentary and/or Presidential records

It is the policy that within 90 days of employment, all employees including senior officials or political appointees, must be briefed regarding the types of records they will be required to protect and the different methods for meeting the Federal guidelines.
all employees including senior officials or political appointees
Prior to leaving employment with USDA, or reporting to a new USDA duty location, all departing employees must follow the clearance procedures in accordance with the provisions of this directive.
Prior to leaving employment with USDA, or reporting to a new USDA duty location

A certification (see Form AD-3001, Documentary Materials Removal/Nonremoval Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement) must be made by the departing employee, contractor, volunteer or political appointee that all Federal records, regardless of media (including social media), have been identified and transferred to the records management liaison or custodian, Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative (COTR), or have been reassigned to another employee.
departing employee, contractor, volunteer or political appointee
Form AD-3001, Documentary Materials Removal/Nonremoval Certification and Non-Disclosure Agreement
The departing employee and the appropriate Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison and Program Manager must sign the certification.
departing employee and the appropriate Agency Records Officer, Staff Office Records Officer or Field Office Records Liaison and Program Manager
The following guidance helps to ensure that only appropriate documentary materials may be removed.
Separation of Personal Papers . Personal papers (as defined in section 6.m) shall be clearly designated as such and shall at all times be maintained separately from the agency’s records.

Partial Federal/Personal Record . If information about personal matters and USDA business appears in the same document, the document shall be copied with the personal information deleted, and the remaining material treated as a Federal record or nonrecord material, as appropriate.
If information about personal matters and USDA business appears in the same document

Use of Labeling . Documentary material labeled “personal,” “confidential,” “private,” or similarly designated, used in the transaction of public business and which meet the definition of a record, are Federal records or nonrecord materials subject to the provisions of pertinent laws and regulations.
The use of a label such as “personal” is not sufficient to determine the record status of documentary materials.
The following types of documentary materials may NEVER be removed:

The only copy of any documentary materials involved in the conduct of the affairs of USDA or any other components of the Federal Government, whether or not judged to be records (including any copy that is unique, for example, because it contains the signature or initials of the writer, reviewers, and/or concurrent parties);
Any documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) the removal of which will create such a gap in the files as to impair the completeness of essential documentation.
Indexes, or other finding aids, necessary for the use of the official files may not be removed;
The only copy of indexes or other finding aids (whether or not judged to be records) that are necessary to the use of office files;
Portions of documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute classified information;
Portions of documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute information subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, 5 U.S.C. § 552a;

Portions of other documentary materials (whether or not judged to be records) that constitute information the disclosure of which is prohibited by law, such as grand jury, tax, and trade secret information.
All other types of nonpublic Federally-owned documentary materials, including privileged materials, may be removed only with specific approval from the appropriate Agency Records Officer.
only with specific approval from the appropriate Agency Records Officer
All other types of nonpublic Federally-owned documentary materials, including privileged materials
Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA may request the following:
Removal of or access to documentary materials that are reasonably related to the requester’s official responsibilities while an employee.
Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA

Maintenance of assembled documentary materials for a specific period of time, not to exceed one year following departure from USDA’s employment, during which he or she may request removal or access pursuant to paragraph 6.c.(1).
Departing or former employees and political appointees of USDA
All records, originals and copies, are under the control of USDA, regardless of how and by whom they were created or obtained.

Removal of documentary material must be approved in accordance with the preceding provisions to ensure that USDA’s ability to claim privileges in litigation, to claim Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) exemptions, and to protect sensitive and classified information.
Personal diaries, which are really private records of public activities, are private property and may be removed.

When matters dealt with in work aids such as office diaries, logs, memoranda of conferences and telephone calls are covered elsewhere by adequate records, such work aids may be removed provided they do not contain information otherwise prohibited from removal.
provided they do not contain information otherwise prohibited from removal
This applies to personal papers created and/or maintained on paper as well as in electronic format.
Extra reference copies may be removed under certain circumstances.
Prior to removal, it must be determined that no legal or policy reason exists that would prevent removal and that the record copy, or other necessary copies, are available in USDA.
If the copy is of a document originating with another agency, the requirements of the originating agency must be determined.

Records will not be disposed of or removed while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, subpoena, litigation or lawsuit under the FOIA or the Privacy Act, as provided for in General Records Schedule 14.
while they are the subject of a pending request, appeal, subpoena, litigation or lawsuit under the FOIA or the Privacy Act

As the head of USDA, the Secretary of Agriculture is vested with the authority to make and preserve records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the agency. (44 U.S.C. 3101.)

The Secretary of Agriculture has delegated to the CIO oversight responsibility for the USDA-wide records disposition program (7 CFR 2.89(a)(10); 2.89(a)(11)(x)).

Within the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), the Associate CIO for Technology Planning, Architecture, and E-Government (TPA&E) is responsible for developing and managing USDA’s records management program.
Associate CIO for Technology Planning, Architecture, and E-Government (TPA&E)
The Associate CIO carries out this responsibility in partnership with USDA’s business and technology communities.

Review proposed USDA reporting and record keeping requirements, including those contained in rules and regulations, to ensure that they impose the minimum burden upon the public and have practical utility for USDA;

Data Quality Act (Pub. L. No. 106-554 § 515) and under the Paperwork Reduction Act (44 U.S.C. 3501-3520), including review of USDA information activities,

The Departmental Records Officer, who is designated by the Associate CIO for TPA&E , is responsible for the leadership, coordination, and oversight of the USDA-wide records management program for the Office of the Secretary:
Serves as the USDA's representative with the National Archives and Records Administration, other Federal agencies, and external organizations on matters pertaining to records management.

Criminal penalties are provided in 18 U.S.C. § 641 (Public Money, Property or Records) and §2071 (Concealment, Removal, or Mutilation of Records) for the unlawful removal or destruction of Federal records.

Criminal penalties are provided in 18 U.S.C. § 793 (Gathering, Transmitting or Losing Defense Information) and § 798 (Disclosure of Classified Information) for the unlawful disclosure, loss, or destruction of certain information pertaining to national defense or national security.
18 U.S.C. § 793 (Gathering, Transmitting or Losing Defense Information)
Other criminal and civil penalties may apply for unlawful disclosure of statutorily confidential information.

The Secretary is required by 44 U.S.C. § 3106 (Unlawful Removal, Destruction of Records) to notify the Archivist of the United States of any actual, impending, or threatened unlawful removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of Federal records in the custody of the Department.

The purpose of this regulation establishes the policy for ensuring that all material created, received or maintained during an employee’s employment or appointee’s tenure with the Federal Government that meets the criteria for a Federal record remains in Federal custody when an employee or appointee departs the Agency. It also reiterates the special consideration given to Presidential Records Retention requirements (44 U.S.C. 22).
